Edit space

Place your study.

Set the location of the property. All times use the UTC offset below.

India is UTC +5.5. For locations with daylight saving, adjust the offset for the date.

Align your camera.

Stand at the centre of the selected space, with the camera 1.6 m above its floor. Hold your phone upright in portrait. Align the centre with a known true bearing and the horizon. Keep it level; roll is not compensated.

65° is an initial estimate, not a lens measurement. Match a known pair of bearings to calibrate the field of view. Sun overlays remain approximate.

Know what the light tells you.

  1. Place the property.

    Use GPS on site or enter coordinates. Verify the time zone.

  2. Measure the surroundings.

    In Floor plan, draw a rectangle for the open space. Set its dimensions and floor elevation. Add buildings, walls, or overhead slabs as blockers with measured positions and heights.

  3. Follow the sun.

    Scrub time or calculate the year. Yellow is unobstructed direct sun; red is shade caused by your model. Hours are area-weighted: half the space lit for two hours equals one sun-equivalent hour.

  4. Check it on site.

    Camera paths use your alignment. A marked opening is a screen annotation on a frozen frame, not a tracked or measured 3D surface. Recording a walk saves video; it does not reconstruct the house.

Accuracy has several parts.

Solar position uses NOAA/Meeus equations. This implementation is not survey-certified. Obstructions are manually modelled boxes; no automatic building detection, terrain, window transmission, reflections, cloud forecast, or video-to-3D reconstruction is included. The camera lens, compass, and measurements need field validation. Do not look directly at the sun to calibrate.

For indoor light, explicitly model walls and ceilings, leaving window openings between separate boxes. An unmodelled wall is treated as open air.

Camera and location are requested only when used. Study geometry is saved in this browser; recordings are downloaded. Export a study to back it up. On iPhone, use Safari’s Share menu and Add to Home Screen.
